articleTitle: 'Impedance match' personal computers with engineers
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The author gives a framework to help judge the merits of personal computer applications and discusses the 'interface impedance' between the engineer and the computer. Just as in electrical circuits, the effective power transfer is optimized when the 'impedance match' is optimum. Different engineers have different 'impedances' and different computer hardware/software configurations have different 'impedances'. Some engineers want to do everything on a computer and some want to do nothing. Some tasks should be done on a computer and some should not be done on computers. The author also gives the software developer guidance in the development of useful programs by looking at end users as a spectrum of talent rather than as users with assumed homogeneous talent.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testing to assure reliable operation of electric motors
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: A discussion is presented of several field test procedures that can be used as part of a motor maintenance program. An outline is also presented of failure mechanisms in motor insulation systems. The application of surge comparison testing is discussed along with an interpretation of test results. Since turn-to-turn shorting is a major factor in causing motor winding failure, a test for impaired turn insulation is a good periodic test for motors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wire and cable update-1990
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The authors address progress and trends in cable designs, applications, and installations. While medium-voltage cable is emphasized, certain types of low-voltage cable are also considered. Improvements in materials and design are discussed for each component part of the cable including the conductor, semiconducting shields, insulation, metallic shield, and protective jacket. Industry standards are considered as they relate to the proper sizing, rating, and construction of cables used in the petrochemical industry. Ampacity tables for medium-voltage as well as low-voltage cable continue to be a controversial issue, and the authors consider the alternatives covered by the 1990 National Electrical Code (NEC). The 1990 NEC still allows industrial users to calculate technically correct ampacities under engineering supervision. IEEE efforts to establish new and comprehensive methods for determining ampacity are also reviewed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Random wound versus form wound on low voltage synchronous generators
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Low-voltage generators, less than 600 V, are presently manufactured in random windings up to 1500 kW. The primary reason for using random coils is to reduce cost and increase the mechanization of manufacturing. Even with expensive epoxy resins and vacuum impregnation, the performance capability and endurance to harsh chemical and environmental conditions of random windings are far inferior to form-wound coils. A discussion is presented of the relative merits of form-wound insulation systems versus random-wound systems, from basic construction through actual field conditions. Applications involving 600 V SCR loads are analyzed in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The benefits of allowing for increased starting current in AC squirrel-cage induction motors
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Opportunities to improve motor efficiency by reducing the present restrictions on the motor starting current are identified. The existing National Electrical Manufacturer's Association (NEMA) standards are reviewed, and a new standard is recommended. The impact on motor operating temperature and power factor is discussed. In those cases where increased starting current is prohibitive, alternative starting methods are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A study of steam vs. electrical pipeline heating costs on a typical petro-chemical plant project
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Two investment studies were made on typical petrochemical plants to compare capital costs for installation of steam and electrical pipeline heating systems. It is found that for the plants studied, the electrical investment is significantly lower. A tool for making such a study on proposed facilities is described and validated by investment studies. Some of the advantages and disadvantages of the two systems, other than economic, are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technical considerations for large AC induction motors on variable frequency applications
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: An examination is made of those issues that must be considered when applying an AC drive. These include the following: (1) motor loading; (2) efficiency and motor losses; (3) load torque requirements and drive capability; (4) motor insulation life; (5) power factor correction; (6) bearing performance; (7) circulating shaft currents; (8) mechanical resonances; and (9) aerodynamic and magnetic noise. The authors argue that conventional induction motor design philosophies need to be modified and matched to controller and load characteristics if optimum performance is to be achieved. This requires that the entire drive system be assessed as a unit. Purchasers must ensure that the subjects addressed in this work are considered by appropriate parties supplying components to the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The ultra efficient amorphous substation transformer
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: A brief description is given of amorphous transformer technology development, and a comparison is made of the technical characteristics and performance to conventional high-efficiency silicon steel transformers. The author addresses how amorphous transformer technology can reduce industrial power losses and improve productivity. It is shown that amorphous transformers have a role in the equation of industrial productivity improvement. Each industrial user must make an independent assessment. Some will derive greater benefits than others. Most will realize some benefits. Benefits are considered to be greatest in the following situations: (1) areas with high electricity costs; (2) when transformer replacement is happening for PCB removal or other reasons; (3) when a plant is being constructed; (4) where transformers are inside and create an added air-conditioning load; (5) where transformers experience seasonal loads or extended low duty cycle; and (6) when overall economics justify replacing existing transformers for efficiency, reliability, or other reasons.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A structured approach to electrical reliability auditing of chemical production facilities
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The chemical industry has, for many years, conducted its own forms of auditing. This structured approach has been adopted simply because it has provided management with a tool that is easily understandable and also allows them to determine where the most improvements can be made for the least expenditure. This structured approach also allows for direct comparison of the various operating units within the total complex. A description is given of each facet of the structured approach. Definitions of the index numbering system used are explained as well as the index average with upper and lower control limits utilized in conjunction with range charts. The author also addresses the types of individuals chosen to perform the auditing, the training utilized, and what kinds of comparative success has ensued.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Controlling starting and stopping pump surges with microprocessor based starter
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Not only are line surges and the fluid hammer effect present when starting pump motors, but in many instances they are also present when stopping these motors. In those cases when normal check valves cannot be used, special hydraulic valves have been used to eliminate these stopping surges. Solid-state reduced-voltage starters have proven helpful in reducing starting surges in certain applications. A solution to stopping the surge and fluid hammer problem can be implemented with normal check valves and solid-state starters using microprocessor-based reduced-voltage starters. A review is presented of application considerations and requirements for applying these specialized motor controllers for eliminating surges on starting and stopping pumps in the petroleum and chemical industry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Programmable controllers integrate oil field SCADA and automation
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: An examination is made of the benefits of oil production supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems which integrate remote terminal unit (RTU) functionality into programmable controller based control systems. This design concept was applied in a west Texas oil field automation project. The major benefits of this SCADA system include a reduction in operating costs due to an increase in the efficiency of operating personnel and a decrease in production downtime. Although the scope of this automation project included other items such as surveillance cameras and instrumentation, the authors focus entirely on the SCADA control system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Revised 515: recommended practice for electrical resistance heat tracing
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Working Group 515 was reinstated to provide specific recommendations for CID1 (Class 1, Division 1) applications and to update the product testing section in view of new heater technologies. The background and rationale for accomplishing these objectives in the revised RP515 are presented. RP515 provides a basis for manufacturers and approval authorities to qualify electrical resistance heaters for unclassified, Class 1, Division 2 and Class 1, Division 1 applications. The design, installation, and maintenance recommendations give the user the means to achieve a safe and reliable heat tracing system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Control of self-regulating heating cable for use in pipeline heating applications
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Self-regulating heating cable is an effective method of electrical heat tracing. The control of temperature without conventional sensors such as RTDs and thermocouples is described. The theory of temperature control using variable self-regulating cable is discussed. Characteristics unique to this method of heat tracing are detailed and a controller specified to meet these requirements. A cost-effective control system is described and laboratory results presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of an innovative self-tuning adaptive controller for complex industrial processes
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: A description is given of the implementation of an adaptive controller that uses an orthogonal function space to represent the plant transfer function. The use of orthogonal filters permits rapid parameter estimation while maintaining robust control under a wide range of operating conditions. A description is also given of the mathematical model the development of a computer algorithm and the results of testing at two industrial sites.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Correlations to Neher-McGrath ampacity calculations for submersible pump cables
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The configuration and application of electric submersible pump cable demands careful consideration of temperature effects on the cable materials. Tests were conducted to develop correlation factors and modifications to the Neher-McGrath thermal model. These disclose the unique features of the cable. A series of equations are presented. Application charts are provided to assist the user in proper selection of the cable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical area classification definitions, applications and alternatives
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: A review is presented of the definitions of Class I, Class II, and Class III locations. A discussion is presented of the differences between Division 1 and 2 locations along with an explanation of the seven groups, A, B, C, D, E, F and G. An explanation of how National Electrical Manufacturer's Association (NEMA) enclosures are to be applied in classified areas is given. Other closely related standards, the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA)-496 'Purged and Pressurized Enclosures for Electrical Equipment' and Instrument Society of America (ISA-RP) 12.6 'Installation of Intrinsically Safe Systems for Hazardous (Classified) Locations', are briefly discussed as to how they can provide alternatives for applications of electrical equipment in classified locations. An application guide is presented along with a partial cross-reference between the National Electrical Code (NEC) and International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC)/European Committee for Electrotechnical Standardization (CENELEC) standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of downhole electric impedance heating systems for paraffin control in oil wells
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Paraffin deposition in oil wells is a problem frequently encountered in the oil industry. Conventional methods such as hot oiling, chemical injection or using scrapers have not always been successful and cost effective. Novel approaches based on electrical technology such as electrical impedance heating offer a practical alternative to conventional methods. Three approaches using such technology are examined. An evaluation of a pilot oil well installation using the latest impedance heating technology is presented. A method of calculating skin effect and hysteresis losses is described. It is concluded that electric impedance heating can be a safe and effective method to control paraffin formation in oil wells; however, the economic viability needs to be assessed for each individual application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Personal computer based design packages for electrical distribution systems
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The advantages of PC-based design packages are apparent through the improved accuracy in design and analysis of electrical distribution systems by using common database files that reduce the possibility of mistakes incurred by erroneous and repetitive transmissions and transcriptions of information. Methods have also been developed that allow engineering workstations and computer-aided design/computer-aided engineering (CAD/CAE) systems to merge data developed by engineers on their desktop PCs. Data such as cable schedules or motor and load lists is portable as output from popular spreadsheet and database programs to larger format engineering drawings via FORTRAN-based data-merging programs. The authors discuss the philosophy of how these design packages are developed, what personnel resources are required for development and implementation, and how various software programs are applied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Safety-related maintenance of explosionproof enclosures for Class I, hazardous locations
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: An overview of the National Electric Code requirements for enclosures for arcing devices in Class I locations is presented, along with the theory of explosionproof protection and the standards applicable to enclosures constructed with that type of protection. Three factors which bear on the satisfactory field performance of such equipment are summarized: installation, environment, and maintenance. Proper maintenance procedures applicable to explosionproof enclosures are suggested, and the results of improper maintenance are demonstrated through highlights of actual laboratory tests.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recommended manufacturing inspections and tests for major electrical equipment
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Recommendations are presented for conducting proper manufacturing inspection procedures and tests of alternating-current (AC) motors, transformers, and certain packaged mechanical equipment. These recommendations will assist the purchaser in identifying tests (normally performed by the manufacturer and others) that should be conducted to gain confidence that equipment will be delivered operable and will meet its requirements. The manufacturer should provide documentation of the certified test data and a statement specifying compliance to the appropriate standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance and reliability improvements for MS3002 and MS5001 turbines in pipeline applications
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Modernization of the MS3002 gas turbine has been accomplished with the application of advanced technology components in redesigned turbine hot sections. Texas Eastern Pipeline Co. began installing these modernization packages in 1986 in an effort to improve the efficiency and reliability of two under-utilized MS5001s and 15 MS3002s each with more than 135000 operating hours of service. A description is given of Texas Eastern's motivations to refurbish units more than 30 years old, including details of the uprate installations and subsequent operating experience.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of process control with programmable controllers
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: This report gives an example of a complex customized system with a programmable logic controller at the heart of the operation. The challenge to the project engineer was threefold: (1) to find suppliers for the parts or sub-systems for a total system that meets the user's process needs; (2) to define the responsibilities of the business partners and team members; and (3) to coordinate the efforts of individuals and companies, across great geographical distances and across international borders. It is shown that the technology of the PLC is stable and solid. Moreover, the trends in development are bringing its functionality ever closer to the needs of the process industry. Few will disagree with the suitability of the hardware choices. The second part of the application problem has now taken a clear path to success. The partnership arrangements have made the use of PLCs in process applications feasible on a large scale. It is no longer necessary to have a large staff of engineering talent to implement sophisticated projects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PC based loop drawing generation
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Generating instrument loop drawings can be easy using PC-based software that provides consistent time saving designs while minimizing errors and maximizing throughput. The application presented provides a tool to maintain loop records and create drawings from a database. Checking is easier, and maintenance of wiring variations is improved for plant operations. Comparisons are made between manual and database-derived loop drawings. The application will run on a DOS-based personal computer with a hard drive. Examples using both AutoCAD or MicroStation and dBASE III Plus are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The interfacing of high voltage switchgear and distributed control system in a large cogeneration facility
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The functional interface between a process-related distributed control system (DCS) and the high-voltage switchgear in a large cogeneration plant was accomplished using a programmable logic controller. A description is given of the project background, the overall system, interface selection considerations, development, and commissioning of this interface. It is shown that the controller was the only single equipment item which could perform all the required functions. Point costs were inexpensive, standard contact ratings were adequate, it was easily programmed, and, of particular importance, the direct data transfer to and from the DCS utilized identical protocol and was field proven.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gas compressor skid wiring specifications
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The classification of areas for electrical installations requires consideration of all aspects of the construction and operation of the equipment involved. For something like a gas compressor skid, this means at least evaluating the mechanical process, gas process, and the electrical implications. If all these aspects are not considered, then those who operate the equipment may find that what they have is not compatible with their needs. This situation is aggravated when there are only limited inspections to ensure continued conformance. The author discusses a specification developed for the wiring on gas compressors and the process by which it was developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design considerations for large AC motors to comply with API Standard 541 Second Edition-special purpose motors
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: API Standard 541, Second Edition, is a comprehensive specification that addresses the design, testing and performance of AC induction motors larger than 250 hp. This specification is the result of collaboration between highly sophisticated users, engineering consultants, and manufacturers. The value of the specification, to the user, is to: (a) provide a better quality motor than was previously available as a standard product; (b) significantly reduce the length of the procurement negotiations by including the major user-specified items in the specification; and (c) reduce the cost and delivery time of this type of motor by standardizing most of the specification requirements. An examination is made of the advantages and disadvantages of purchasing a motor under this specification, and a description is also given of the resulting impact on costs and deliveries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonmetallic equipment for hazardous (classified) locations-the IEC approach
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The use of nonmetallics in hazardous locations containing electrical equipment offers significant benefits. However, this concept has rarely been used in traditional National Electrical Code (NEC) and Canadian Electrical Code (CEC) approaches toward hazardous locations. Technology developed through the application of International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standards has more fully exploited the advantages of nonmetallics in hazardous locations specifically when corrosive environments are present. A discussion is presented of the inherent benefits of combining IEC technology with nonmetallics in NEC applications. IEC classifications of the hazards in various electrical systems are compared to NEC and CEC classifications. IEC protection techniques are briefly described, and protection component designs are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Need for industry standards for A-C induction motors intended for use with adjustable frequency controllers
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: With the increased use and variety of A-C induction motors on adjustable frequency controls, there is a need to develop industry standards to provide the guidance necessary for the proper selection of the motor which will function as intended with the control. These standards should establish requirements for both electrical and mechanical characteristics of the motor necessary to establish uniformity within the industry. The authors discuss the reasons why certain topics must be covered by such standards and present proposals for the content.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Maintaining safe electrical work practices in a competitive environment
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The efforts of one corporation to maintain electrical safety performance are described. Basic electrical hazards are reviewed and a flow chart method of categorizing hazardous electrical tasks is presented. A matrix is provided to select appropriate personal protective equipment and identify procedural requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Noise in induction motors-causes and treatments
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: This work consists of three parts. The first part identifies causes and frequencies of windage and magnetic noise in an induction motor. Specific problems that are unique to various motors are also identified. In the second part, a testing procedure is established that can be followed to determine the full load noise level of an induction motor. Also included is a testing procedure to determine the nature and origin of the noise so that it can be treated in the proper manner. In the third part of the work, the most effective methods of reducing motor noise levels in the field and at the factory are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Risk of ignition due to transition currents in medium voltage motors for classified locations
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Research into arcing and sparking at the joints of the enclosure of a two-pole 13.2 kV motor and measurements which basically apply to all 1000 RPM and above machines of multisection enclosure design are described. In the presence of a flammable vapor, the current transfers at enclosure joints are a potential ignition source. These eddy currents in the enclosure are created by stray fields emerging from the active part of the motor consisting of stator and rotor. On the basis of the investigations, necessary remedial measures for large high-speed (1000 RPM and above) motors are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Using new technology to improve reliability of an industrial cable distribution system
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The service history of medium-voltage power cables on the US plant sites of a major industrial manufacturer from 1961 through 1990 is summarized. In past years, this company tended to be reactive, using specifications, diagnostic testing and maintenance practices to manage the reliability of their cable distribution systems. Several technologies in insulation systems, terminations, splices, and installation techniques, introduced in recent years, have allowed a more proactive stance to be taken. In addition, because of some specific failure problems, a highly qualified in-house team has been formed to evaluate existing and future technologies and insulation materials to assure a reliable cable system. A brief review is presented of the new technology, reliability programs, and the accelerated cable life test.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluating computer programs for analyzing industrial power systems: what users need to know
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Computer programs for analyzing industrial electrical power systems are available from many sources. The lack of suitable test standards or problems to evaluate their accuracy and performance has left the user with this burden. Verification by hand may be extremely difficult or impossible. A description is given of procedures for evaluating software accuracy, performance, and user friendliness. Examples used are limited to power flow and short circuit algorithms which depict linear and nonlinear solution techniques. These programs have been singled out because they are the most widely used in industry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electric utility regulation: procedures, parameters and current issues from an intervenor's perspective
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: The purpose of this work is to describe the regulatory process, specifically: (1) Who decides what the rates will be and how? (2) Can industrial users participate in the process, and, if so, how? (3) What basic factors determine the rates? and (4) What are some of the current issues that could affect future electricity rates? Some of the key issues being debated today that have had or may have an impact on electric rates include: (1) imprudence, (2) used and useful, (3) cost sharing, (4) phase-in, and (5) innovative rates. Each of these issues is briefly examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: API Standard 546-a new purchase specification for large synchronous motors and generators
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: API Standard 546, Form-Wound Brushless Synchronous Motors, is a purchase specification for synchronous motors and generators. Background information is given on the creation of the standard. An overview is also provided of the major electrical and mechanical design features, accessories, and testing requirements. The user's and supplier's views on the need for the standard are presented. Applications of various synchronous machine constructions are summarized. Contributions of the standard to reliability, particularly in the areas of mechanical vibration and rotor dynamics, are emphasized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Compliance with EPA PCB regulations-options analysis
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: An outline is presented of factors involved in mitigating PCB problems. These factors cover the following topics: understanding EPA regulations, such as the requirements of the EPA spill policy, the fires rule, the less-than-50-p.p.m. rule, and the notification and manifesting rule; determining the present situation by performing a risk appraisal to study each PCB-containing device to determine service record, fluid integrity, spill consequences, outage requirements, electrical and mechanical condition and current application; assessing the corporate attitude to determine if the company has a management attitude geared toward environmental issues, PCBs in particular; and studying the options, which range from doing nothing to retrofill or retrofit. A brief discussion is presented of the evolution of present EPA PCB regulatory requirements. Options for managing PCBs are also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Record of Conference Papers. Industry Applications Society 37th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference (Cat. No.90CH2922-3)
publicationTitle: 37th Annual Conference on Petroleum and Chemical Industry
abstract: Presents the front cover of the proceedings record.
